findings.affected_surface: D-Bus interface introspection/org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.Device.xml SetManaged method argument type changed from boolean to uint32
findings.old_behavior: The SetManaged D-Bus method accepted (boolean managed, uint32 flags) as input parameters. D-Bus signature was (bu). Any D-Bus client could call SetManaged(TRUE/FALSE, flags) using the boolean type.
findings.new_behavior: The SetManaged D-Bus method now accepts (uint32 managed, uint32 flags). D-Bus signature changed to (uu). The managed parameter accepts 0=NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_NO, 1=NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_YES, or 2=NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET.
findings.compatibility_reason: D-Bus is strict about type signatures. Any existing client sending (bu) will receive a D-Bus TYPE_MISMATCH error because the expected signature is now (uu). This breaks backward compatibility for all D-Bus clients of the SetManaged method, including libnm users and direct D-Bus callers.

evidence.snippet: <arg name="managed" type="b" direction="in"/> -> <arg name="managed" type="u" direction="in"/>

findings.why_not_internal_only: The introspection XML defines the D-Bus interface contract consumed by all D-Bus peers. The handler and client-side changes implement this protocol change. D-Bus is the primary control interface for NetworkManager.
findings.uncertainty: None - the D-Bus signature change is explicit in both the introspection XML and the implementation.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that all known consumers (libnm, nmcli, gnome-control-center, plasma-nm) have been updated to use the new (uu) signature.
findings.test_recommendation: Test SetManaged with old signature (bu) fails with TYPE_MISMATCH. Test (uu) with values 0, 1, 2 all work. Test both RUNTIME and PERMANENT flag combinations.

findings.affected_surface: Public libnm API nm_device_set_managed_async parameter type gboolean -> NMDeviceManaged
findings.old_behavior: nm_device_set_managed_async() accepted gboolean (int) for the managed parameter. Callers could pass TRUE/FALSE or any integer value.
findings.new_behavior: nm_device_set_managed_async() accepts NMDeviceManaged enum. Callers must use NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_NO, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_YES, or NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET.
findings.compatibility_reason: gboolean and C enum are both int-sized, so ABI compatibility is preserved. However, source compatibility is broken: existing code passing gboolean literals (TRUE/FALSE) will fail to compile. The old deprecated synchronous API nm_device_set_managed(gboolean) is preserved as a migration path.

evidence.snippet: gboolean managed -> NMDeviceManaged managed in function definition

findings.why_not_internal_only: nm-device.h is an installed public header distributed as part of libnm development packages.
findings.uncertainty: Compiler behavior depends on -Wenum-conversion flags. Some compilers may only warn.
findings.recommended_review: Check that all in-tree callers of nm_device_set_managed_async have been updated to use NMDeviceManaged enum values.
findings.test_recommendation: Compile existing code using nm_device_set_managed_async to verify compiler warnings. Test that old gboolean values still produce correct behavior (TRUE=1=YES, FALSE=0=NO).

findings.affected_surface: New public enum NMDeviceManaged type definition in public header
findings.old_behavior: No NMDeviceManaged type existed. The device managed state was represented as gboolean (TRUE=managed, FALSE=unmanaged) or raw int.
findings.new_behavior: New public enum NMDeviceManaged with values NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_NO=0, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_YES=1, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET=2. The RESET=2 value triggers restoring device managed state to default.
findings.compatibility_reason: Purely additive new type definition. Backward compatible at source and binary level. Old gboolean values (0=FALSE, 1=TRUE) map directly to NO (0) and YES (1). Code using switch/case on managed values with a default branch may encounter new RESET=2 value.

evidence.snippet: typedef enum { NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_NO = 0, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_YES = 1, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET = 2, } NMDeviceManaged;

findings.why_not_internal_only: nm-dbus-interface.h is an installed public header distributed as part of libnm-core development packages.
findings.uncertainty: Code using switch/managed with default branch may encounter unexpected RESET=2.
findings.recommended_review: Check if any consumers use switch/case on managed values with default that might misinterpret RESET=2.
findings.test_recommendation: Test that NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_NO(0) and NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_YES(1) produce identical behavior to old gboolean TRUE/FALSE. Test NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET(2) properly resets state.

findings.affected_surface: New runtime state reset behavior when NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET is used via SetManaged D-Bus call
findings.old_behavior: In the RUNTIME flag path, the managed property was set directly via g_object_set(self, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED, !!managed, NULL). Only TRUE=managed or FALSE=unmanaged were valid inputs.
findings.new_behavior: When managed == NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET (2), the runtime state is reset by forgetting the NM_UNMANAGED_USER_EXPLICIT flag via nm_device_set_unmanaged_by_flags with NM_UNMAN_FLAG_OP_FORGET, clearing previously set explicit unmanaged state.
findings.compatibility_reason: The RESET=2 value is additive - old callers never send this value, so there is no backward compatibility break. The behavior for old values 0 and 1 is preserved exactly. Callers using the new RESET value must understand the resulting device state transition.

evidence.snippet: if (managed == NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET) { nm_device_set_unmanaged_by_flags(self, NM_UNMANAGED_USER_EXPLICIT, NM_UNMAN_FLAG_OP_FORGET, ...); } else { g_object_set(self, NM_DEVICE_MANAGED, !!managed, NULL); }

findings.why_not_internal_only: set_managed is a static function but is called from impl_device_set_managed which is the registered D-Bus method handler. Any D-Bus caller sending RESET triggers this new behavior.
findings.uncertainty: The exact device state after reset depends on interaction of multiple unmanaged flags which may vary by device type.
findings.recommended_review: Review the interaction between NM_UNMANAGED_USER_EXPLICIT forgetting and the overall unmanaged flag system.
findings.test_recommendation: Test SetManaged with NM_DEVICE_MANAGED_RESET via D-Bus and verify device returns to default managed state. Test with both PERMANENT and RUNTIME flags.
